findings.F1: In calm markets the brief's effect is present on both sides together. A day's move in units of its 30-day swing is followed by a 5-day excess return the same way of +1.52 % (t 2.75 with same-day cases summed; 771 cases on 195 days), and the slope is +1.74 % per swing unit (t 4.82). In agitated markets the same measure is +0.03 % (t 0.03; 587 cases), with a slope of -0.01 % per unit.
findings.F2: In calm markets the follow-through grows with the day's size. By quartile of |day's return / 30-day std| it runs from +0.80 % (t 1.12) in the lowest to +2.66 % (t 2.57, 86 days) in the highest. Measured from the next day's close, the highest quartile gains +4.08 % over 5 days (t 3.47) against +0.87 % in the lowest.
findings.F3: The tested idea took only down days, and that is why it fell short. Calm down days follow through by +1.56 % (t 1.97, 141 days) and calm up days by +1.47 % (t 1.58, 125 days, slope t 2.68). The verdict's down-only main measure had t 1.59, and its median split failed (-0.25), because the forecast is standardised over 60 values rather than read in raw swing units.
findings.F4: The calm follow-through is broad rather than carried by one slice:
findings.F5: The effect needs days to show. In calm markets it is +0.25 % at 3 days (t 0.72), +1.52 % at 5 days (t 2.75) and +1.54 % at 10 days (t 1.36), where the slope per swing unit is 2.03 % (t 2.87).
findings.F6: In calm markets, where a day closes inside its own range predicts the next 5 days, graded. By quartile of close location (0 = at the low, 1 = at the high) the 5-day excess return is -2.73 % (t -2.72), +0.07 %, +0.66 % and +1.47 %. In a joint fit it adds +1.58 % per unit of close location on top of the swing-scaled move, which adds +1.44 % per unit.
findings.F7: The close-location effect turns over in agitated markets. There, low-close days are followed by +0.91 % over 5 days (t 0.85) and high-close days by -1.45 % (t -1.28), the reverse of the calm reading in F6.
findings.F8: Two other patterns stand out but repeat ideas the profile map already holds, so I leave them out:

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's one-day return against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its return in the same direction over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In calm markets, a trader follows a day that stands out against the coin's recent swing, long after a large up day and short after a large down day, with more size the larger the day.
ideas.name: calm big day follows through

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's one-day return against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger its return in the same direction over the 5 days that start one day after it.
ideas.consequence: A trader who misses the first day of a calm-market breakout can still join it the next day in the same direction, and the larger the day, the more is left to gain.
ideas.name: calm big day delayed follow

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the nearer a coin's daily close sits to the day's low within its high-low range, the lower its return over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: In calm markets a close near the day's low is a reason to sell or stay out, and a close near the high a reason to hold, which is the opposite of the low-close rebound held in agitated markets.
ideas.name: calm close location continues
